evidence_quotes.quid_pro_quo: Rep skips directly into 'Yeah, you're just looking to move a couple of things or what are we looking at?' with no time-box framing or promise of a dependable quote.
evidence_quotes.their_agenda: Never asked. Rep launches into item listing ('Yeah, that definitely helps. Yeah, what would they be?') without asking about concerns or what answers the customer wants.
evidence_quotes.estimate_anchor: Rep gives hourly rate ($208/hour, $520 minimum, ~$567 for this job) but does not tie it to typical range for this home size or personalize it to the customer's stated concerns—just raw pricing.
evidence_quotes.damage_coverage_delivered: Rep mentions '$2,000 per move' and 'no worries damage coverage' but frames it vaguely as 'higher evaluation' and 'go well above and beyond 60¢ per pound'—does not explicitly state 'no deductible / no fine print' or that it's built into the rate, not an add-on.
evidence_quotes.explicit_ask: Rep never asks 'Would you like our help with your move?' Instead, customer initiates: 'we're definitely interested on what day can we book you all for?' The ask happens in reverse, unprompted by the rep.
evidence_quotes.final_concerns_check: Rep asks 'any other questions while we're on the phone'—empty throwaway phrasing, not the genuine 'What's still concerning you about this move?' version.

top_strength: Calvin efficiently gathered the specific items to be moved, confirmed addresses and contact details accurately, and booked the appointment with clear time windows—logistics execution was clean.
coaching_note: You skipped the entire structure of Section 1 (quid pro quo / time-box framing), never asked their concerns or agenda in Section 2, gave a quote with no real personalization or reflection, and never asked for the business—the customer had to ask you; reorient every call to follow the script sections in order, starting with 'This will take 10–15 minutes and you can walk away with a quote you can depend on. Does that sound good?'
